lines.text: In 1784, a French architect designed a monument... about the size of the Las Vegas Sphere.

shots.prompt: A colossal smooth stone sphere resting on a tiered circular base ringed with tall dark cypress trees, tiny 18th-century figures at its foot, dramatic sky.
shots.motion: Camera pulls back and rises to reveal the full size of the colossal sphere, cypress trees swaying, clouds drifting. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

lines.text: A hollow sphere... one hundred and fifty metres across.

shots.prompt: A vast stone sphere seen from below its curve, people in 18th-century clothes tiny beside it, cypress trees, morning mist.
Architectural cross-section style painting of a giant hollow sphere on a stepped base, warm parchment tones, neoclassical.
A single small stone sarcophagus alone on the floor of an immense dark spherical hall, a shaft of light falling on it.

lines.text: By day, sunlight through tiny holes...

shots.prompt: Inside a colossal dark stone sphere, hundreds of thin beams of daylight shining through tiny holes in the curved ceiling.
shots.motion: Beams of sunlight slowly shift and shimmer through the tiny holes, dust floating in the light. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

lines.text: ...would turn it into a sky full of stars.

shots.prompt: The inside of an immense dark dome glittering with thousands of points of light like a star-filled night sky, a tiny figure standing below.

lines.text: At night, a glowing orb would hang inside... like a sun.

shots.prompt: A huge glowing orb suspended in the centre of a vast dark spherical hall, lighting the curved stone walls golden, a tiny visitor below.
shots.motion: The glowing orb pulses softly, golden light rippling across the curved walls. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

shots.prompt: An empty misty field at dawn with a few cypress trees, no monument, 18th-century countryside, quiet.

lines.text: Almost two hundred and forty years later... Las Vegas built one almost the same size.

shots.prompt: A giant glowing spherical entertainment venue at night in a desert city, its surface lit with colourful light, crowds below, generic modern design.
An old neoclassical sphere design and a modern glowing sphere side by side at dusk, the same size, desert and cypress trees blending.

lines.text: Now imagine standing inside the original.

shots.prompt: A lone visitor standing on the floor of a colossal stone sphere whose dome is filled with glittering starlight, awe-inspiring scale.
shots.motion: Slow upward crane from the tiny visitor toward the star-filled dome, the points of light twinkling. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

# Short #006 - Boullée's Cenotaph for Newton

## Title options (1 = recommended)
1. The Las Vegas Sphere Was Designed in 1784
2. In 1784, an Architect Designed a Sphere for Isaac Newton
3. The 150-Metre Sphere That Turned Day Into Night

## Description
A hollow sphere 150 metres across. By day, sunlight through tiny holes turned the inside into a sky full of stars. By night, a giant glowing orb hung in the centre.

French architect Étienne-Louis Boullée designed this cenotaph for Isaac Newton in 1784. It was never built. Almost 240 years later, a sphere of nearly the same size opened in Las Vegas. This is a concept visualization of what might have been.

Visuals are AI-generated concept art, not photographs or plans of a real structure.

- Physics World: "The Las Vegas Sphere and its curious link with Isaac Newton"
- Wikipedia: Étienne-Louis Boullée
